body:
> This aims to close #100112 by using a more accurate evaluation of size_changed and pos_changed, as suggested by @kleonc .

To be precise, in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/100112#issuecomment-2525053605 I haven't suggested any solution, just pinpointed the cause.

---

Currently this PR basically reverts #93908, hence it would reintroduce/reopen #93832 and #48935.

Indeed the size recalculation can introduce floating point errors, but AFAICT the root cause of #93832/#48935 is that the size is being recalculated (and hence checked whether it has changed) when it shouldn't be done at all. E.g. if I'd have a plain Control not anyhow anchored etc., then changing its `position` shouldn't cause size recalculation like it currently does, it shouldn't even be checked whether `size` has changed. See the `_size_changed()` being called here:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/b24656090f8ab38d4939a49e75cde83c984ab779/scene/gui/control.cpp#L1392-L1409

So to me it seems like the logic for trigerring size recalculation etc. would need to be tweaked/rethinked in the first place. Note that's quite fundamental though, so potential changes seem regression prone (hence should be rather done early in the dev phase (like we currently are for 4.5)). Anyway, this seems out of scope of this PR.

Whether this PR should be merged as is depends on what do we conside worse: 
- #93832
- and #48935,

or:
- #100112.

To me it makes sense to revert #93908 (merge this PR) and find different fix for #93832/#48935.

That makes sense for me too, but I'll spend some time tomorrow looking for a way to solve the two issues you mentioned. This doesn't seem like an easy problem.

I have to sleep now, but I'll look into it tomorrow.

It agree with you (from my limited knowledge of the codebase) that the best way to solve this is to find another way to calculate the control size/pos.

I won't be changing this PR, as you have said, fixing the other two regressions are out of the scope of this one. 

There appears to only be one commit too, so I don't think there's anything to squash either.
